purpose: Final staging semantics store for Pilot 1 (7 drugs). Holds 100% verbatim source atomic bullets, exact source-declared flags, agent-derived candidate flags, and canonical consumption references.

source_board_items: Vitamin K antagonist.
Narrow therapeutic window; INR monitoring is a classic association.
Major/fatal bleeding is the central toxicity.
Diet, drugs, and supplements can alter anticoagulant effect.
Course mnemonic associates warfarin with warfare against Vitamin K.
Warfarin: vitamin K pathway + INR monitoring.
DOAC Xa inhibitors: -xaban; no routine INR titration.
Antiplatelet drugs such as clopidogrel act on platelets, not vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors.
Course provenance: Pharmacology Summary.md, cardiovascular/anticoagulant section around L398-L405.
source_clinical_impact_statements: Bleeding/bruising: high clinical relevance.
Lab interpretation: INR is essential to therapy management.
Falls/trauma matter more because occult or overt bleeding can be more consequential.
Sudden diet/supplement changes can matter.
Do not interpret bruising or bleeding tendency without considering anticoagulant therapy.
Medication use should be visible before needling intensity/depth decisions.
Acupuncture card should present a bleeding-risk prompt, not a universal no acupuncture rule.
INR / clinical bleeding assessment per prescribing team.
canonicalized_or_consumed_source_items: Mechanism: Reduces functional vitamin K-dependent coagulation-factor synthesis.
Indications: Venous thromboembolism, pulmonary embolism, atrial fibrillation, cardiac valve replacement.
Boxed warning: Major/fatal bleeding risk and regular INR monitoring stressed.
Mnemonic: Warfare against Vitamin K.
Classic association: Warfarin -> Vitamin K antagonist -> INR monitoring & Bleeding risk.

source_board_items: -xaban -> factor Xa inhibitor.
Main clinical danger: bleeding.
Do not abruptly discontinue without appropriate anticoagulation planning: current label warns of increased thrombotic risk.
Neuraxial/spinal procedures carry spinal/epidural hematoma risk.
Mnemonic from course logic: XABAN -> Xa.
source_clinical_impact_statements: Bleeding/bruising risk.
Stopping anticoagulation prematurely can expose the patient to thrombotic risk.
Any planned neuraxial procedure has a specific label warning.
Display bleeding_risk. Ask about unusual bruising/bleeding and co-use of other anticoagulant/antiplatelet agents.
Do not tell patients to hold prescribed anticoagulation for acupuncture.
canonicalized_or_consumed_source_items: Mechanism: Direct inhibition of factor Xa reduces thrombin generation.
Indications: Nonvalvular AF stroke reduction, DVT prophylaxis, DVT/PE treatment.
Boxed warning: Premature discontinuation thrombotic risk & neuraxial hematoma risk.
Mnemonic: -XABAN indicates Factor Xa inhibitor.
Exam trap: Routine INR not required, but spinal/epidural hematoma warning applies.

source_board_items: Antiplatelet, not the same mechanism as warfarin/DOACs.
Course mnemonic: P in clopidogrel / aspirin -> platelets.
Requires metabolic activation, especially through CYP2C19.
Current boxed warning focuses on reduced antiplatelet effect in CYP2C19 poor metabolizers.
Bleeding remains a major clinical safety concern.
source_clinical_impact_statements: Bruising/bleeding may be medication related.
Genetics/drug interactions affecting CYP2C19 may reduce efficacy.
Visible antiplatelet flag; adjust clinical caution to actual bleeding history and overall hemostatic context rather than applying an automatic ban.
canonicalized_or_consumed_source_items: Mechanism: Prodrug converted to active metabolite that inhibits P2Y12 ADP receptors.
Indications: Acute coronary syndrome, recent MI, recent stroke, PAD.
Boxed warning: Reduced antiplatelet effect in CYP2C19 poor metabolizers.
Mnemonic: Clopidogrel blocks P2Y12 ADP receptors on platelets.
Classic association: Clopidogrel -> P2Y12 ADP receptor inhibitor -> Antiplatelet effect.

source_board_items: One drug can appear under more than one Board lens.
NSAID: prostaglandin/COX pathway, pain/inflammation.
Low-dose use: antiplatelet context.
Course emphasizes gastric irritation/erosion, hemorrhage, renal injury, and Reye syndrome risk in children with viral illness.
Compare with acetaminophen: analgesic/antipyretic but not a classic anti-inflammatory NSAID.
source_clinical_impact_statements: High-value card because patients commonly combine aspirin with fish oil, supplements, or herbs.
Each interaction must be graded by evidence; blood-moving alone is not proof of a clinically significant interaction.
canonicalized_or_consumed_source_items: Mechanism: Irreversible inhibition of COX-1.
Indications: Analgesia, antipyresis, anti-inflammatory, ACS, TIA, stroke.
Mnemonic: Irreversible COX-1 inhibitor antiplatelet.
Exam trap: Reye syndrome risk in children/teens with viral illness.

source_board_items: Injectable anticoagulant; distinguish from oral warfarin and oral DOACs.
Major practical issue: bleeding.
Often appears in perioperative, thromboembolism, pregnancy/fertility or recurrent-loss medical contexts when prescribed.
source_clinical_impact_statements: Medication should trigger a bleeding/bruising review and awareness of injection-site bruising.
canonicalized_or_consumed_source_items: Mechanism: Low-Molecular-Weight Heparin (LMWH).
Indications: DVT prophylaxis and treatment, unstable angina/non-Q-wave MI.
Mnemonic: Low Molecular Weight Heparin (LMWH).
Exam trap: Monitored via anti-Factor Xa levels, NOT routine aPTT.

source_board_items: -SARTAN -> ARB.
Blocks angiotensin II receptor signaling.
Think: hypertension, diabetic nephropathy context, hyperkalemia, renal function, hypotension.
Current label has boxed warning for fetal toxicity.
Compare ACE inhibitor -pril: ARB avoids ACE inhibition but still shares RAS-related potassium, renal and pregnancy issues.
Course provenance: the course uses valsartan as the ARB prototype and explicitly links -sartan with hyperkalemia. Losartan appears mainly in the legacy pregnancy-category table.
source_clinical_impact_statements: Potential medication contribution: dizziness;
Potential medication contribution: low BP, especially with volume depletion;
Potential medication contribution: renal function deterioration;
Potential medication contribution: elevated potassium.

If a patient with dizziness or weakness is taking losartan plus a diuretic, Clinical Impact should surface BP/volume/electrolyte context before symptoms are assigned entirely to a TCM deficiency pattern.
canonicalized_or_consumed_source_items: Mechanism: Selectively blocks angiotensin II binding to AT1 receptors.
Indications: Hypertension, Diabetic nephropathy, Stroke risk reduction.
Boxed warning: Fetal toxicity (injury and death to developing fetus).
Mnemonic: -SARTAN indicates ARB. Think: hypertension, diabetic nephropathy, hyperkalemia, and fetal toxicity.
Exam trap: ARBs avoid ACEi cough but share fetal toxicity & hyperkalemia risk.

source_board_items: Thiazide diuretic.
Course mnemonic: See No Evil and the high-yield association with secondary angle-closure glaucoma.
Classic electrolyte associations: hypokalemia, hyponatremia and other volume/electrolyte changes.
Compare: furosemide -> loop, stronger diuresis, ototoxicity association; spironolactone -> potassium-sparing, hyperkalemia; HCTZ -> thiazide, hypokalemia/hyponatremia.
Course provenance: Pharmacology Summary.md around L401; detailed diuretic material also exists in Pharm+OM+Winter+2019+W5-diuretics.md.
source_clinical_impact_statements: Potential medication contribution: cramps / weakness;
Potential medication contribution: dizziness / hypotension;
Potential medication contribution: confusion in electrolyte disturbance;
Potential medication contribution: acute eye pain / visual change in secondary angle-closure glaucoma.
Leg cramps, fatigue, weakness and dizziness are exactly the kind of symptoms that can be over-attributed to Qi/Blood deficiency if medication/electrolyte effects are not visible.
canonicalized_or_consumed_source_items: Mechanism: Thiazide diuretic inhibiting NaCl reabsorption in distal convoluted tubule.
Indications: Hypertension, Edema.
Mnemonic: Thiazide diuretic. See No Evil -> secondary angle-closure glaucoma & hypokalemia/hyponatremia.
Exam trap: Hypokalemia, hyponatremia, hyperuricemia (gout flare), and rare acute myopia/secondary angle-closure glaucoma.
